title: MCP Apps: Extending the Frontier — Ido Salomon & Liad Yosef
talk_summary: This is a spec/evangelism talk about MCP Apps (formerly MCP-UI), a protocol extension for transmitting interactive HTML/UI resources from MCP servers into chat hosts, with a standardized app-to-host callback flow.

takeaways.what_they_do: An MCP tool call can be linked to a resource containing HTML; the host renders it in a sandbox and the app communicates back to the host via a callback that recommends tool calls, with the host retaining control of the flow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that tool call is actually linked to a resource ... it's just a resource with a uh some prefix

takeaways.what_they_do: The app never calls its backend directly; it sends an event to the host, which decides whether to invoke the recommended tool, keeping the host in control of the flow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's actually sending a message to the host saying, "Hey, user clicked a button. Do something with it."
